summary: The candidate is a substantial partial fix: it passes its focused regressions and independently fixes one-character streaming fragmentation, streaming singular-marker stripping, a simple unclosed-section overflow, and explicit reset. It does not fully resolve the original issue because an earlier complete call masks an oversized unclosed later call from the one-time safety check, leaving over-limit state buffered even after finish(), and the non-streaming public path still does not recognize singular K2-Thinking section markers.

tests.what_was_measured: Recorded-base reproduction: one-character fragmentation produced zero calls and leaked the complete wire format; singular streaming markers leaked; a 200-character unclosed call remained buffered; no reset method existed.
Candidate regression suite: 67 passed, 7 subtests passed.
Existing parser integration unit coverage: 6 passed, 237 deselected.

Independent adversarial cases. One-character and singular-marker streaming passed; simple overflow flushed. A complete first call plus oversized unclosed second call retained 269 characters with section_max=128, and finish() retained the same buffer. Singular markers in detect_and_parse produced no calls and leaked all markers.
Confirmed tests imported candidate source from /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/function_call/kimik2_detector.py rather than an installed wheel.

gpu_execution.evidence: One gfx950-compatible ROCm device was visible through torch, but no GPU execution was used because the changed code is a deterministic Python string parser and no model weights were available.

remaining_counterexamples: With SGLANG_KIMI_PARSER_SECTION_MAX=128, one increment containing a complete first tool call followed by an unclosed second call with 200 argument characters bypasses the entry-time safety check because the buffer contains the first call's end marker. The candidate emits call fragments for both calls and retains 269 characters; BaseFormatDetector.finish() emits nothing and leaves all 269 characters buffered.

detect_and_parse/has_tool_call still only recognize <|tool_calls_section_begin|>. A complete singular K2-Thinking wire format using <|tool_call_section_begin|>/<|tool_call_section_end|> returns zero calls and leaks the complete marked text as normal content.
remaining_limitations: No Kimi-K2 or Kimi-K2.5 weights were available, so actual model token emission, semantic tool accuracy, HTTP client behavior, and multi-node behavior were not tested.
The candidate changes only Python; repository-environment.json specifies native=null and wheel=null, so no native rebuild applies.
The configured section limit is implemented with Python character count although candidate prose describes bytes; multibyte-memory behavior was not used as a rejection basis.
Serving code constructs a parser per response choice, so cross-request reuse is not the normal inspected serving path. Direct reuse remains stateful unless the caller explicitly invokes reset().
